D.2 Single-Table Completeness

We begin with the foundational case of a single table. Let the database contain only one table TT with columns 𝒞⁡(T)={c1,…,cm}\mathcal{C}(T)=\{c_{1},\dots,c_{m}\}. Let 𝒱⁡(T)\mathcal{V}(T) denote its (finite) set of rows. For any row r∈𝒱⁡(T)r\in\mathcal{V}(T) and column c∈𝒞⁡(T)c\in\mathcal{C}(T), the corresponding cell instance is v=(r,c)v=(r,c) and its value is denoted by AvA_{v} (Definition D.1).

To describe the data-generating process, we introduce a generic row random vector

𝐀≔(A1,…,Am),where ​Ak​ represents the value of column ​ck​ in a random row.\mathbf{A}\coloneqq(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}),\qquad\text{where }\mathrm{A}_{k}\text{ represents the value of column }c_{k}\text{ in a random row.}

Thus, a realized row rr corresponds to one sample 𝐚r=(ar,1,…,ar,m)\mathbf{a}_{r}=(a_{r,1},\dots,a_{r,m}) from the joint distribution P⁡(𝐀)P(\mathbf{A}). Equivalently, for each column ck∈𝒞⁡(T)c_{k}\in\mathcal{C}(T) we have A(r,ck)=ar,kA_{(r,c_{k})}=a_{r,k}, and Ak\mathrm{A}_{k} denotes the random value of column ckc_{k} in a generic row.

Assumption D.4 (Row i.i.d.).

Rows in table TT are independent and identically distributed draws from a fixed row distribution:

𝐚r∼i.i.d.P(𝐀)for all r∈𝒱(T).\mathbf{a}_{r}\sim_{i.i.d.}P(\mathbf{A})\qquad\text{for all }r\in\mathcal{V}(T).
Justification

Assumption D.4 formalizes the standard single-table modeling view used throughout classical statistics and most tabular learning benchmarks: a table is treated as a multiset of records drawn from a common population distribution. This perspective is also implicit in early tabular foundation model constructions such as prior-data fitted networks (e.g., TabPFNv1, TabICL), where a dataset-level generative mechanism is sampled once (e.g., an SCM with parameters θSCM\theta_{\mathrm{SCM}}), and then individual rows are generated independently by drawing fresh exogenous noise for each row. In this view, the table exhibits a global mechanism shared across all rows within the dataset, while randomness arises from per-row noise, making rows exchangeable and (under the simplest setting) i.i.d. We emphasize that this i.i.d. assumption is a baseline used to build intuition and establish a clean completeness result. Many real-world tables deviate from i.i.d. sampling due to temporal ordering, distribution shift, repeated measurements, or group-level correlations, and are already attempted to be handled by later work (e.g., TabPFNv2). However, these extensions are orthogonal to the core message here: in the simplest and most widely used single-table setting, an SCM-style shared mechanism with independent per-row noise yields the i.i.d. formulation captured by Assumption D.4.

Lemma D.5 (Universal measurable conditional sampler + approximation transfer).

Let (X,Y)(X,Y) be random variables with YY taking values in a standard Borel space (e.g., ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}, any countable set, any finite set, or a product of these). Then there exists a Borel measurable function ff and an independent U∼Unif⁡(0,1)U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that

Y​=𝑑​f​(X,U).Y\ \overset{d}{=}\ f(X,U).

Moreover, if f^n\hat{f}_{n} is any sequence of measurable functions such that f^n​(X,U)→f⁡(X,U)\hat{f}_{n}(X,U)\to f(X,U) in probability under the joint law of (X,U)(X,U), then

f^n​(X,U)⇒f⁡(X,U).\hat{f}_{n}(X,U)\Rightarrow f(X,U).
Proof sketch.

The first statement is a standard randomization lemma for regular conditional distributions on standard Borel spaces: sample YY by applying a measurable map to (X,U)(X,U). The second statement follows from the Continuous Mapping Theorem / Slutsky-style arguments on pushforward measures: convergence in probability of the outputs implies weak convergence of the output laws. ∎

Theorem D.6 (Single-Table SCM Completeness).

Fix any joint distribution P⁡(A1,…,Am)P(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}) satisfying Assumption D.4, and fix any ordering (A1,…,Am)(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}). Assume each Ak\mathrm{A}_{k} takes values in a standard Borel space (so that a conditional CDF and generalized inverse are well-defined; e.g., discrete sets or subsets of ℝ\mathbb{R}). Then there exist measurable functions

fk:val(A<k)×[0,1]→val(Ak),k=1,…,m,f_{k}:\ \mathrm{val}(\mathrm{A}_{<k})\times[0,1]\to\mathrm{val}(\mathrm{A}_{k}),\qquad k=1,\dots,m,

and independent noise variables Uk∼Unif⁡(0,1)U_{k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that the SCM

Ak=fk(A<k,Uk),k=1,…,m,\mathrm{A}_{k}=f_{k}(\mathrm{A}_{<k},U_{k}),\qquad k=1,\dots,m,

induces exactly the joint distribution P⁡(A1,…,Am)P(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}).

Moreover, if f^k\hat{f}_{k} are chosen from universal approximator classes (for the relevant notion of approximation under the input distribution), then the SCM with f^k\hat{f}_{k} can approximate P⁡(A1,…,Am)P(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}) to arbitrary precision in distribution.

Proof sketch.

Fix an ordering (A1,…,Am)(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}). By the chain rule,

P⁡(A1,…,Am)=∏k=1mP⁡(Ak∣A<k).P(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m})=\prod_{k=1}^{m}P(\mathrm{A}_{k}\mid\mathrm{A}_{<k}).

Apply Lemma D.5 to each conditional: for every kk there exists a measurable fkf_{k} and independent Uk∼Unif⁡(0,1)U_{k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that

Ak​=𝑑​fk​(A<k,Uk).\mathrm{A}_{k}\ \overset{d}{=}\ f_{k}(\mathrm{A}_{<k},U_{k}).

Composing these samplers yields an SCM that reproduces the target joint distribution.

For approximation, choose f^k\hat{f}_{k} from a universal approximator class so that f^k​(A<k,Uk)→fk​(A<k,Uk)\hat{f}_{k}(\mathrm{A}_{<k},U_{k})\to f_{k}(\mathrm{A}_{<k},U_{k}) in probability under the induced input law. Iterating Lemma D.5 (approximation transfer) over k=1,…,mk=1,\dots,m implies that the induced joint distribution converges to P⁡(A1,…,Am)P(\mathrm{A}_{1},\dots,\mathrm{A}_{m}). ∎

D.3 Multi-Table Completeness

We now extend the single-table analysis to a full relational database with multiple tables. Our goal is to characterize and approximate the joint distribution of all cell values in an RDB.

In the single-table setting, the set of variables (columns) is fixed. In the relational setting, however, the set of variables and their allowed link structure depend on the schema. Formally, the schema graph GSG_{S} (Definition 3.3) specifies which tables exist and which foreign-key relations are permitted. Given GSG_{S} and the row sets {𝒱⁡(T)}T∈𝒯\{\mathcal{V}(T)\}_{T\in\mathcal{T}}, the set of cell instances 𝒱={(r,c):r∈𝒱(T),c∈𝒞(T)}\mathcal{V}=\{(r,c):r\in\mathcal{V}(T),\,c\in\mathcal{C}(T)\} is well-defined (Definition D.1). We therefore consider the conditional joint distribution over all cell values,

P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱|GS).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\,\middle|\,G_{S}\right).
Three-stage decomposition.

We instantiate the same Schema →\to Structure →\to Content decomposition as in the main text (Eq. equation 1), and adopt consistent stage numbering:

  • •

    Stage 1 (Schema): sample a schema graph GSG_{S}.

  • •

    Stage 2 (Structure): generate the structural skeleton of the instance, including key columns 𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t={Av}v∈𝒱s​t​r​u​c​t\mathcal{D}_{struct}=\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{struct}} (Definition D.2) and, optionally, latent row states 𝒵={Zr}r∈𝒱i​n\mathcal{Z}=\{Z_{r}\}_{r\in\mathcal{V}_{in}} (Definition D.3). The realized structure induces (or equivalently includes) the instance graph Gi​nG_{in}.

  • •

    Stage 3 (Content): generate all remaining feature values 𝒟d​e​p={Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p\mathcal{D}_{dep}=\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}} conditioned on the realized structure (and GSG_{S}).

Accordingly, by the chain rule we write the database distribution as

P(𝒟)=P⁡(GS)⏟Stage 1: Schema⋅P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)⏟Stage 2: Structure⋅P⁡(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)⏟Stage 3: Content.P(\mathcal{D})=\underbrace{P(G_{S})}_{\text{Stage 1: Schema}}\cdot\underbrace{P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})}_{\text{Stage 2: Structure}}\cdot\underbrace{P(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})}_{\text{Stage 3: Content}}.
Stage 1 (schema) as a modular prior.

We treat P⁡(GS)P(G_{S}) as an external schema prior (hand-designed or learned). Since our focus is on instance generation conditioned on GSG_{S}, we do not further analyze Stage 1 beyond assuming it can represent distributions over finite schema DAGs.

What remains to prove.

We focus on the completeness of Stage 3 (Content) and Stage 2 (Structure). Following the roadmap stated earlier, we prove Stage 3 first because it reduces to approximating local conditional mechanisms with structured aggregation over relational neighborhoods; we then reuse this result inside the Stage 2 proof, which introduces an additional selection mechanism for generating foreign-key links.

D.3.1 Stage 3: Conditional Feature Generation (Content Completion)

Setting.

Fix a schema GSG_{S}. Suppose Stage 2 has generated the structural skeleton 𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t={Av}v∈𝒱s​t​r​u​c​t\mathcal{D}_{struct}=\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{struct}} (Definition D.2) and latent row states 𝒵={Zr}r∈𝒱i​n\mathcal{Z}=\{Z_{r}\}_{r\in\mathcal{V}_{in}} (Definition D.3). Given (GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t)(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct}), the instance graph Gi​nG_{in} is induced by referential integrity (Definition 3.3). Stage 3 models the conditional distribution of all dependent feature values:

P({Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p|𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}}\,\middle|\,\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S}\right).

For brevity, let

C2≔(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)(equivalently, ​C2=(Gi​n,𝒵,GS)​).C_{2}\coloneqq(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})\quad\text{(equivalently, }C_{2}=(G_{in},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})\text{)}.

We use the dependent feature types 𝒜d​e​p\mathcal{A}^{dep} and dependent cell instances 𝒱d​e​p\mathcal{V}^{dep} as defined in Definition D.2. For each feature type a∈𝒜d​e​pa\in\mathcal{A}^{dep} define its instance set

𝒱ad​e​p≔{v∈𝒱d​e​p:ColumnOf⁡(v)=a}.\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}\coloneqq\{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}:\ \mathrm{ColumnOf}(v)=a\}.

A naive autoregressive factorization over all v∈𝒱d​e​pv\in\mathcal{V}^{dep} is generally intractable. We therefore introduce a hierarchical factorization based on feature types, with locality defined relative to the fixed instance graph Gi​nG_{in} and the structural states 𝒵\mathcal{Z}.

Assumption D.7 (Feature-Type Ordering).

There exists a global topological ordering 𝒪=(a1,…,aM)\mathcal{O}=(a_{1},\dots,a_{M}) of all dependent feature types 𝒜d​e​p\mathcal{A}^{dep}.

Assumption D.8 (Typewise Conditional Independence).

Given C2C_{2} and all dependent features from preceding types {Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}} (where a′≺aa^{\prime}\prec a denotes precedence in the global order 𝒪\mathcal{O}, and 𝒱<ad​e​p≔⋃a′≺a𝒱a′d​e​p\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}\coloneqq\bigcup_{a^{\prime}\prec a}\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a^{\prime}}), the dependent feature instances of the current type aa are conditionally independent:

P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱ad​e​p∣C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p)=∏v∈𝒱ad​e​pP⁡(Av∣C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}\mid C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right)=\prod_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}P\!\left(A_{v}\mid C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right).
Assumption D.9 (Structured Local Dependency).

For each dependent cell instance v∈𝒱d​e​pv\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}, there exists a parent set P​a​(v)⊆𝒱s​t​r​u​c​t∪𝒱<ColumnOf⁡(v)d​e​pPa(v)\subseteq\mathcal{V}^{struct}\cup\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<\mathrm{ColumnOf}(v)} such that

P⁡(Av∣C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ColumnOf⁡(v)d​e​p)=P⁡(Av∣{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v)).P\!\left(A_{v}\mid C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<\mathrm{ColumnOf}(v)}}\right)=P\!\left(A_{v}\mid\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right).

Moreover, P​a​(v)Pa(v) is relationally local: every u∈P​a​(v)u\in Pa(v) lies either in the same row as vv or in a row within kk hops of RowOf⁡(v)\mathrm{RowOf}(v) in Gi​nG_{in} (for a fixed constant kk). Here 𝒱<ColumnOf⁡(v)d​e​p\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<\mathrm{ColumnOf}(v)} denotes the union of dependent cell instances whose feature types precede ColumnOf⁡(v)\mathrm{ColumnOf}(v) in the global order 𝒪\mathcal{O}.

Corollary D.10 (Hierarchical Factorization for Stage 3).

Under Assumptions D.7–D.9, the Stage 3 conditional distribution factorizes as

P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p∣C2)=∏a∈𝒪∏v∈𝒱ad​e​pP⁡(Av∣{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v)).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}}\mid C_{2}\right)=\prod_{a\in\mathcal{O}}\ \prod_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}P\!\left(A_{v}\mid\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right).
Proof.

By the chain rule applied over the feature-type order 𝒪\mathcal{O} (Assumption D.7),

P({Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p∣C2)=∏a∈𝒪P({Av}v∈𝒱ad​e​p|C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}}\mid C_{2}\right)=\prod_{a\in\mathcal{O}}P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}\,\middle|\,C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right).

By typewise conditional independence (Assumption D.8),

P({Av}v∈𝒱ad​e​p|C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p)=∏v∈𝒱ad​e​pP(Av|C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p).P\!\left(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}\,\middle|\,C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right)=\prod_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}}P\!\left(A_{v}\,\middle|\,C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right).

Finally, by structured local dependency (Assumption D.9), for each v∈𝒱ad​e​pv\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a} we have

P(Av|C2,{Au}u∈𝒱<ad​e​p)=P(Av|{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v)),P\!\left(A_{v}\,\middle|\,C_{2},\{A_{u}\}_{u\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{<a}}\right)=P\!\left(A_{v}\,\middle|\,\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right),

which yields the stated factorization. ∎

Assumption D.11 (Mechanism Sharing by Type).

All dependent feature instances of the same type share an identical conditional mechanism. That is, for each a∈𝒜d​e​pa\in\mathcal{A}^{dep}, there exists a conditional distribution KaK_{a} such that

P⁡(Av∣{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v))=Ka​(Av∣{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v))∀v∈𝒱ad​e​p.P\!\left(A_{v}\mid\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right)=K_{a}\!\left(A_{v}\mid\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right)\qquad\forall\,v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}.
Assumption D.12 (Hierarchical Parent Processing).

The mechanism KaK_{a} must process the parent set P​a​(v)Pa(v) in a way that respects the RDB hierarchy. Let Rv≔{RowOf⁡(u):u∈P​a​(v)}R_{v}\coloneqq\{\mathrm{RowOf}(u):u\in Pa(v)\} be the set of unique parent rows and Tv≔{TableOf⁡(u):u∈P​a​(v)}T_{v}\coloneqq\{\mathrm{TableOf}(u):u\in Pa(v)\} the set of unique parent tables.

  • •

    (a) Intra-row coherence (ordered). For each parent row r∈Rvr\in R_{v}, the parent cells from that row, {u∈P​a​(v):RowOf⁡(u)=r}\{u\in Pa(v):\mathrm{RowOf}(u)=r\}, must be processed in a fixed canonical order. The row latent ZrZ_{r} may be injected as an additional “row token” in this ordered processing.

  • •

    (b) Inter-row invariance (unordered). Within each parent table T∈TvT\in T_{v}, the mechanism must be permutation-invariant to the order of row-level representations coming from rows r∈𝒱⁡(T)∩Rvr\in\mathcal{V}(T)\cap R_{v}.

  • •

    (c) Inter-table coherence (ordered). The mechanism must process the table-level representations for tables in TvT_{v} in a fixed canonical order (e.g., a fixed schema order or a topological order induced by GSG_{S}).

Corollary D.13 (Hierarchical SCM Architecture with Latents).

Under Assumptions D.11 and D.12, each mechanism KaK_{a} can be realized by an SCM faf_{a} that computes AvA_{v} via bottom-up hierarchical aggregation over P​a​(v)Pa(v), with row-latent injection:

Av\displaystyle A_{v} =fa​(P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v),Uv)=fa′​(zv,Uv),\displaystyle=f_{a}(Pa(v),Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)},U_{v})=f_{a}^{\prime}(z_{v},U_{v}), (2)
zr=hrow(Concat(Zr,[Au:u∈Pa(v),RowOf(u)=r])),\displaystyle z_{r}=h^{\mathrm{row}}\!\left(\mathrm{Concat}\bigl(Z_{r},\ [A_{u}:\ u\in Pa(v),\ \mathrm{RowOf}(u)=r]\bigr)\right), (3)
zT\displaystyle z_{T} =Aggtable({zr:r∈Rv,r∈𝒱(T)}),\displaystyle=\mathrm{Agg}^{\mathrm{table}}\!\left(\{z_{r}:\ r\in R_{v},\ r\in\mathcal{V}(T)\}\right), (4)
zv\displaystyle z_{v} =hglobal​(Concat⁡({zT:T∈Tv},ZRowOf⁡(v))).\displaystyle=h^{\mathrm{global}}\!\left(\mathrm{Concat}\bigl(\{z_{T}:\ T\in T_{v}\},\ Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\bigr)\right). (5)

Here hrowh^{\mathrm{row}} and hglobalh^{\mathrm{global}} are order-sensitive functions (e.g., MLPs over concatenations), and Aggtable\mathrm{Agg}^{\mathrm{table}} is permutation-invariant (e.g., Deep Sets).

Proof.

This is constructive. Eq. equation 3 enforces ordered intra-row processing (AD.12a) and allows injecting the row latent ZrZ_{r} as additional row-level context. Eq. equation 4 aggregates row representations within each table in a permutation-invariant manner (AD.12b). Eq. equation 5 processes table representations in canonical order (AD.12c) and can additionally condition on the target row latent ZRowOf⁡(v)Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}. ∎

Theorem D.14 (Completeness of Stage 3 (Content Completion)).

Let P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p∣C2)P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}}\mid C_{2}) satisfy Assumptions D.7–D.12. Then there exist hierarchical SCMs {f^a}a∈𝒜d​e​p\{\hat{f}_{a}\}_{a\in\mathcal{A}^{dep}} of the form in Corollary D.13 and independent noises Uv∼Unif⁡(0,1)U_{v}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that

Av=f^ColumnOf⁡(v)​(P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v),Uv),v∈𝒱d​e​p,A_{v}=\hat{f}_{\mathrm{ColumnOf}(v)}(Pa(v),Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)},U_{v}),\qquad v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep},

approximates P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱d​e​p∣C2)P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}}\mid C_{2}) arbitrarily well in distribution.

Proof.

Step 1 (Reduction to local mechanisms). By Corollary D.10, it suffices to approximate each local conditional kernel

Ka​(Av∣{Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v))(v∈𝒱ad​e​p).K_{a}\!\left(A_{v}\mid\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\right)\qquad(v\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}).

Step 2 (Sampling representation + approximation transfer). Fix a type aa and a cell instance v∈𝒱ad​e​pv\in\mathcal{V}^{dep}_{a}. Let

Xv≔({Au}u∈P​a​(v),ZRowOf⁡(v)),Yv≔Av.X_{v}\coloneqq\Bigl(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa(v)},\,Z_{\mathrm{RowOf}(v)}\Bigr),\qquad Y_{v}\coloneqq A_{v}.

By Lemma D.5, there exists a measurable sampler faf_{a} and an independent Uv∼Unif⁡(0,1)U_{v}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that

Av​=𝑑​fa​(Xv,Uv).A_{v}\ \overset{d}{=}\ f_{a}(X_{v},U_{v}).

Moreover, if f^a​(Xv,Uv)→fa​(Xv,Uv)\hat{f}_{a}(X_{v},U_{v})\to f_{a}(X_{v},U_{v}) in probability under the induced input law of XvX_{v}, then f^a​(Xv,Uv)⇒fa​(Xv,Uv)\hat{f}_{a}(X_{v},U_{v})\Rightarrow f_{a}(X_{v},U_{v}).

Step 3 (Existence of f^a\hat{f}_{a} within the hierarchical SCM class). Assumptions D.11–D.12 restrict faf_{a} to be hierarchy-respecting in its dependence on P​a​(v)Pa(v): ordered within each parent row, permutation-invariant over parent rows within a table, and ordered across tables. The architecture in Corollary D.13 is universal for this function class because: (i) hrowh^{\mathrm{row}} and hglobalh^{\mathrm{global}} are chosen from universal approximator classes for order-sensitive maps, and (ii) Aggtable\mathrm{Agg}^{\mathrm{table}} is chosen from a universal permutation-invariant set-function class. Therefore, there exists a sequence f^a\hat{f}_{a} in this architecture such that f^a​(Xv,Uv)→fa​(Xv,Uv)\hat{f}_{a}(X_{v},U_{v})\to f_{a}(X_{v},U_{v}) in probability under the induced input law.

Step 4 (Joint convergence of Stage 3). Approximating each factor in the product of Corollary D.10 and using independence of {Uv}\{U_{v}\} yields convergence of the induced joint Stage 3 conditional distribution. ∎

Connection to the practical GNN decoder.

The Stage 3 proof is stated in terms of a hierarchy-respecting conditional mechanism KaK_{a}. In the main model, we implement this mechanism by a bidirectional relational GNN over Gi​nG_{in} with a shared decoder. This choice is compatible with the proof: message-passing layers compute permutation-equivariant summaries of kk-hop neighborhoods, and the decoder realizes the final conditional sampling step.

Proposition D.15 (GNN as an instantiation of Stage 3 mechanisms).

For any fixed hop radius kk, a kk-layer relational message passing network with permutation-invariant aggregation can approximate the bounded-hop, permutation-equivariant neighborhood summaries required by Corollary D.13, under standard expressivity conditions on the per-relation MLPs and an injective set aggregator.

Proof sketch.

Both constructions compute row-wise representations by composing (i) order-sensitive intra-row processing and (ii) permutation-invariant aggregation across sets of neighbors, repeated over a bounded-hop neighborhood. Universal approximation of the constituent MLPs yields approximation of the resulting neighborhood-to-representation map, and the decoder then approximates the conditional output distribution using standard inverse-transform/categorical sampling. ∎

D.3.2 Stage 2: Structural Generation (Keys, Links, and Latent States)

Setting.

Fix a schema GSG_{S}. Stage 2 models P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}), where 𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t\mathcal{D}_{struct} are structural cells (Definition D.2) and 𝒵={Zr}r∈𝒱i​n\mathcal{Z}=\{Z_{r}\}_{r\in\mathcal{V}_{in}} are optional row latents (Definition D.3). For convenience we denote the key-cell subsets

𝒱p​k≔{(r,c)∈𝒱:c∈⋃T∈𝒯𝒦p​k​(T)},𝒱f​k≔{(r,c)∈𝒱:c∈⋃T∈𝒯𝒦f​k​(T)},𝒱c​o​n​n≔{(r,c)∈𝒱:c∈𝒞c​o​n​n},\mathcal{V}^{pk}\coloneqq\{(r,c)\in\mathcal{V}:c\in\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal{T}}\mathcal{K}^{pk}(T)\},\quad\mathcal{V}^{fk}\coloneqq\{(r,c)\in\mathcal{V}:c\in\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal{T}}\mathcal{K}^{fk}(T)\},\quad\mathcal{V}^{conn}\coloneqq\{(r,c)\in\mathcal{V}:c\in\mathcal{C}^{conn}\},

so that 𝒱s​t​r​u​c​t=𝒱p​k∪𝒱f​k∪𝒱c​o​n​n\mathcal{V}^{struct}=\mathcal{V}^{pk}\cup\mathcal{V}^{fk}\cup\mathcal{V}^{conn}. To keep notation light, the completeness argument below is written for the common case 𝒞c​o​n​n=∅\mathcal{C}^{conn}=\emptyset (i.e., 𝒱c​o​n​n=∅\mathcal{V}^{conn}=\emptyset); the extension to 𝒞c​o​n​n≠∅\mathcal{C}^{conn}\neq\emptyset follows by including 𝒱c​o​n​n\mathcal{V}^{conn} among the generated structural cells and in the structural context Ctx⁡(⋅)\mathrm{Ctx}(\cdot) defined below.

Stage 3 conditions on a fixed realized structure and models feature values via local parent sets P​a​(v)Pa(v) at the cell level. Stage 2, in contrast, must model the structure itself (FK links), which naturally introduces (i) a schema-respecting generation order (to satisfy referential integrity) and (ii) possible competition/degree effects among parent rows. Accordingly, Stage 2 mirrors Stage 3’s five-assumption style (ordering, locality, sharing, structured processing), but replaces Stage 3’s within-type conditional independence with a restricted dependence on a permutation-invariant competition summary.

Assumption D.16 (Deterministic Primary Keys).

For each table TT with nT≔|𝒱⁡(T)|n_{T}\coloneqq|\mathcal{V}(T)| rows, primary key values are a deterministic, known injective encoding of row identity. Concretely, there exists a known injective map PKEncT:{1,…,nT}→val⁡(𝒦p​k​(T))\mathrm{PKEnc}_{T}:\{1,\dots,n_{T}\}\to\mathrm{val}(\mathcal{K}^{pk}(T)) such that the PK cells of the ii-th row equal PKEncT​(i)\mathrm{PKEnc}_{T}(i). Hence PK values carry no causal/content information beyond identifying rows.

Under Assumption D.16, Stage 2 reduces to modeling the joint distribution of (i) all foreign-key cells (equivalently, the induced instance graph Gi​nG_{in}), and (ii) the latent row states 𝒵\mathcal{Z}:

P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)=P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱f​k,𝒵∣GS),withGi​n=g⁡(GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t).P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})=P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{fk}},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}),\quad\text{with}\quad G_{in}=g(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct}).

For each dependent table TT, fix a row order πT=(rT,1,…,rT,nT)\pi_{T}=(r_{T,1},\dots,r_{T,n_{T}}). If TT has parent tables Par⁡(T)={Tp(1),…,Tp(p)}\mathrm{Par}(T)=\{T_{p}^{(1)},\dots,T_{p}^{(p)}\}, define for each row rT,kr_{T,k} the selected parent-row tuple

UT,k=(uT,k(1),…,uT,k(p)),uT,k(j)∈𝒱⁡(Tp(j)).U_{T,k}=(u_{T,k}^{(1)},\dots,u_{T,k}^{(p)}),\qquad u_{T,k}^{(j)}\in\mathcal{V}(T_{p}^{(j)}).

For source tables (no FKs), UT,kU_{T,k} is taken to be empty. For a dependent table TT with parents Par⁡(T)={Tp(1),…,Tp(p)}\mathrm{Par}(T)=\{T_{p}^{(1)},\dots,T_{p}^{(p)}\}, define the feasible parent-tuple set

𝒞T≔𝒱(Tp(1))×⋯×𝒱(Tp(p)),\mathcal{C}_{T}\coloneqq\mathcal{V}(T_{p}^{(1)})\times\cdots\times\mathcal{V}(T_{p}^{(p)}),

so that UT,k∈𝒞TU_{T,k}\in\mathcal{C}_{T}. (For finite instances, 𝒞T\mathcal{C}_{T} is finite.)

Assumption D.17 (Table Topological Order).

There exists a topological ordering of tables Topo⁡(GS)=(T(1),…,T(N))\mathrm{Topo}(G_{S})=(T^{(1)},\dots,T^{(N)}) such that every foreign-key edge in GSG_{S} points from an earlier table to a later table.

Assumption D.17 implies a valid procedural generation order: parent tables can be sampled before child tables, and each dependent row selects parent rows and copies their PKs into FK cells. For a source table (no FKs), we generate its rows’ latent states from exogenous noise. For a dependent table TcT_{c} with parent tables Par⁡(Tc)={Tp(1),…,Tp(p)}\mathrm{Par}(T_{c})=\{T_{p}^{(1)},\dots,T_{p}^{(p)}\}, each new child row selects a tuple of parent rows (u(1),…,u(p))(u^{(1)},\dots,u^{(p)}) and sets its FK values accordingly. This selection is the structural “routing” mechanism.

Assumption D.18 (Structured Local Dependency).

Fix a dependent table TT with row order πT=(rT,1,…,rT,nT)\pi_{T}=(r_{T,1},\dots,r_{T,n_{T}}) and parent tables Par⁡(T)={Tp(1),…,Tp(p)}\mathrm{Par}(T)=\{T_{p}^{(1)},\dots,T_{p}^{(p)}\}.

For each step kk, let 𝒞T,k⊆𝒞T\mathcal{C}_{T,k}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{T} be a finite candidate-tuple set, where 𝒞T=𝒱(Tp(1))×⋯×𝒱(Tp(p))\mathcal{C}_{T}=\mathcal{V}(T_{p}^{(1)})\times\cdots\times\mathcal{V}(T_{p}^{(p)}).

Define:

  • •

    (Pre-selection context parents). A set P​ac​t​x​(T,k)Pa^{ctx}(T,k) of structural cell instances drawn only from already-generated tables/rows (tables earlier than TT, and rows {rT,j}j<k\{r_{T,j}\}_{j<k} in TT), restricted to a bounded-hop neighborhood (radius k0k_{0}) in the partially constructed instance graph.

  • •

    (Candidate-local parents). For each candidate tuple c∈𝒞T,kc\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}, a set P​ac​a​n​d​(c)Pa^{cand}(c) of structural cell instances drawn from the rows in cc and their bounded-hop neighborhoods (radius k0k_{0}) in the partially constructed instance graph (again, only using already-generated variables).

  • •

    (Embeddings). A context embedding CtxT,k=ΦTc​t​x​({Au}u∈P​ac​t​x​(T,k))\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k}=\Phi^{ctx}_{T}(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa^{ctx}(T,k)}) and candidate embeddings ϕT,k​(c)=ΦTc​a​n​d​({Au}u∈P​ac​a​n​d​(c))\phi_{T,k}(c)=\Phi^{cand}_{T}(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa^{cand}(c)}).

Let ST,k−1=S⁡({UT,j}j<k)S_{T,k-1}=S(\{U_{T,j}\}_{j<k}) be a permutation-invariant competition/degree summary of previous selections.

(Markov restriction). The local conditional depends on the past only through these pre-selection quantities:

P(UT,k,ZrT,k∣all previously generated variables)=P(UT,k,ZrT,k|CtxT,k,{ϕT,k(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1).P(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}\mid\text{all previously generated variables})=P\!\Big(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}\,\Big|\,\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},S_{T,k-1}\Big).

For source tables, interpret UT,kU_{T,k}, 𝒞T,k\mathcal{C}_{T,k}, and ST,k−1S_{T,k-1} as empty and keep only P⁡(ZrT,k∣CtxT,k)P(Z_{r_{T,k}}\mid\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k}).

Assumption D.19 (Mechanism Sharing by Table/Relation Pattern).

For each table TT, all rows share the same conditional mechanism for producing (UT,k,ZrT,k)(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}) from their pre-selection inputs. Concretely, there exists a (table-specific) kernel KTK_{T} such that for all kk,

P(UT,k,ZrT,k|CtxT,k,{ϕT,k(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1)=KT(UT,k,ZrT,k|CtxT,k,{ϕT,k(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1).P\!\Big(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}\,\Big|\,\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},S_{T,k-1}\Big)=K_{T}\!\Big(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}\,\Big|\,\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},S_{T,k-1}\Big).
Assumption D.20 (Hierarchy-Respecting Processing for Structure).

The kernel KTK_{T} processes (i) the context parents P​ac​t​x​(T,k)Pa^{ctx}(T,k) and (ii) each candidate parent set P​ac​a​n​d​(c)Pa^{cand}(c) in a hierarchy-respecting way:

  • •

    (Row-level order). Within any row, structural cells (and optional row latents) are processed in a fixed canonical order.

  • •

    (Within-table set invariance). Within any table, sets of row representations are aggregated permutation-invariantly.

  • •

    (Across-table order). Tables are processed in a fixed canonical order (e.g., schema/topological order).

  • •

    (Candidate-tuple role order). Within a candidate tuple c=(u(1),…,u(p))c=(u^{(1)},\dots,u^{(p)}), the pp parent roles are processed in the canonical FK-role order induced by the schema (so the tuple embedding is sensitive to role).

  • •

    (Candidate-set symmetry). The dependence of KTK_{T} on the candidate set {ϕT,k​(c)}c∈𝒞T,k\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}} is permutation-equivariant with respect to reordering candidates (e.g., implemented by scoring each candidate with a shared function and normalizing).

Corollary D.21 (Stage 2 Factorization (Structure)).

Under Assumptions D.16, D.17, D.18, and D.19, the Stage 2 distribution admits an autoregressive factorization over tables and (within each table) rows:

P({Av}v∈𝒱f​k,𝒵∣GS)=∏T∈Topo⁡(GS)∏k=1nTP(ZrT,k,UT,k|CtxT,k,{ϕT,k(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1),P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{fk}},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})=\prod_{T\in\mathrm{Topo}(G_{S})}\ \prod_{k=1}^{n_{T}}P\!\Big(Z_{r_{T,k}},U_{T,k}\ \Big|\ \mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},S_{T,k-1}\Big),

where UT,kU_{T,k}, 𝒞T,k\mathcal{C}_{T,k} and ST,k−1S_{T,k-1} are empty for source tables.

Proof.

Fix a topological table order Topo⁡(GS)=(T(1),…,T(N))\mathrm{Topo}(G_{S})=(T^{(1)},\dots,T^{(N)}) (Assumption D.17). For each table T(i)T^{(i)}, fix a row order πT(i)=(rT(i),1,…,rT(i),ni)\pi_{T^{(i)}}=(r_{T^{(i)},1},\dots,r_{T^{(i)},n_{i}}). Under Assumption D.16, primary keys are deterministic, so the Stage 2 randomness is fully captured by

Yi,k≔(UT(i),k,ZrT(i),k),Y_{i,k}\ \coloneqq\ (U_{T^{(i)},k},\,Z_{r_{T^{(i)},k}}),

where UT(i),kU_{T^{(i)},k} is empty for source tables.

Step 1 (Repeated chain rule over the nested order).

Applying the chain rule repeatedly over the nested order “tables then rows” gives

P({Av}v∈𝒱f​k,𝒵∣GS)=P({Yi,k}i,k∣GS)=∏i=1N∏k=1niP(Yi,k|GS,all variables generated before (i,k)).P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{fk}},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})=P(\{Y_{i,k}\}_{i,k}\mid G_{S})=\prod_{i=1}^{N}\ \prod_{k=1}^{n_{i}}P\!\left(Y_{i,k}\ \middle|\ G_{S},\ \text{all variables generated before }(i,k)\right).
Step 2 (Apply the candidate-based Markov restriction).

By Assumption D.18, for each dependent-table step (i,k)(i,k) the conditional distribution of Yi,k=(UT(i),k,ZrT(i),k)Y_{i,k}=(U_{T^{(i)},k},Z_{r_{T^{(i)},k}}) given all previously generated variables depends on the past only through: (i) the pre-selection context embedding CtxT(i),k\mathrm{Ctx}_{T^{(i)},k}, (ii) the candidate set 𝒞T(i),k\mathcal{C}_{T^{(i)},k} and its candidate embeddings {ϕT(i),k​(c)}c∈𝒞T(i),k\{\phi_{T^{(i)},k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T^{(i)},k}}, and (iii) the within-table competition summary ST(i),k−1=S⁡({UT(i),j}j<k)S_{T^{(i)},k-1}=S(\{U_{T^{(i)},j}\}_{j<k}). Hence,

P(Yi,k|GS,all variables generated before (i,k))=P(Yi,k|CtxT(i),k,{ϕT(i),k(c)}c∈𝒞T(i),k,ST(i),k−1),P\!\left(Y_{i,k}\ \middle|\ G_{S},\ \text{all variables generated before }(i,k)\right)=P\!\Big(Y_{i,k}\ \Big|\ \mathrm{Ctx}_{T^{(i)},k},\{\phi_{T^{(i)},k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T^{(i)},k}},S_{T^{(i)},k-1}\Big),

with the convention that for source tables UT(i),kU_{T^{(i)},k}, 𝒞T(i),k\mathcal{C}_{T^{(i)},k}, and ST(i),k−1S_{T^{(i)},k-1} are empty, so the right-hand side reduces to conditioning on CtxT(i),k\mathrm{Ctx}_{T^{(i)},k} only.

Step 3 (Substitute into the chain rule product).

Substituting the above identity into the product from Step 1 yields

P⁡({Av}v∈𝒱f​k,𝒵∣GS)=∏i=1N∏k=1niP⁡(Yi,k|CtxT(i),k,{ϕT(i),k​(c)}c∈𝒞T(i),k,ST(i),k−1),P(\{A_{v}\}_{v\in\mathcal{V}^{fk}},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})=\prod_{i=1}^{N}\ \prod_{k=1}^{n_{i}}P\!\Big(Y_{i,k}\ \Big|\ \mathrm{Ctx}_{T^{(i)},k},\{\phi_{T^{(i)},k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T^{(i)},k}},S_{T^{(i)},k-1}\Big),

which is exactly the claimed factorization after re-indexing (i,k)(i,k) back to (T,k)(T,k). ∎

A universal selective SCM.

We now give a constructive parameterization that can realize the Stage 2 factorization (Corollary D.21) while respecting Assumption D.20. Fix a dependent table TT and row step kk with candidate set 𝒞T,k⊆𝒞T\mathcal{C}_{T,k}\subseteq\mathcal{C}_{T} (in the idealized proof one may take 𝒞T,k=𝒞T\mathcal{C}_{T,k}=\mathcal{C}_{T}).

For each row rT,kr_{T,k} we: (i) sample an initial latent ZrT,k(0)Z^{(0)}_{r_{T,k}} from exogenous noise; (ii) compute a hierarchy-respecting pre-selection context embedding

zT,kc​t​x≔CtxT,k=ΦTc​t​x​({Au}u∈P​ac​t​x​(T,k));z^{ctx}_{T,k}\coloneqq\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k}\;=\;\Phi^{ctx}_{T}\!\left(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa^{ctx}(T,k)}\right);

(iii) compute candidate-tuple embeddings for each c∈𝒞T,kc\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k} by

ϕT,k​(c)=ΦTc​a​n​d​({Au}u∈P​ac​a​n​d​(c));\phi_{T,k}(c)\;=\;\Phi^{cand}_{T}\!\left(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa^{cand}(c)}\right);

(iv) score and sample a parent tuple UT,k∈𝒞T,kU_{T,k}\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k} using a shared scoring function gg and a uniform selector:

ℓc=g⁡(ZrT,k(0),zT,kc​t​x,ϕT,k​(c),ST,k−1),c∈𝒞T,k,\ell_{c}=g\!\left(Z^{(0)}_{r_{T,k}},\ z^{ctx}_{T,k},\ \phi_{T,k}(c),\ S_{T,k-1}\right),\qquad c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k},
UT,k=Sample⁡(Softmax⁡({ℓc}c∈𝒞T,k),UT,ks​e​l),UT,ks​e​l∼Unif⁡(0,1);U_{T,k}=\mathrm{Sample}\!\left(\mathrm{Softmax}(\{\ell_{c}\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}}),\,U^{sel}_{T,k}\right),\quad U^{sel}_{T,k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1);

we then set the FK cell values of rT,kr_{T,k} to match the selected parent rows’ PKs (referential integrity); and (v) update the latent state via a universal map ψ\psi:

ZrT,k=ψ⁡(ZrT,k(0),zT,kc​t​x,ϕT,k​(UT,k),UT,kl​a​t),UT,kl​a​t∼Unif⁡(0,1),Z_{r_{T,k}}=\psi\!\left(Z^{(0)}_{r_{T,k}},\ z^{ctx}_{T,k},\ \phi_{T,k}(U_{T,k}),\ U^{lat}_{T,k}\right),\quad U^{lat}_{T,k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1),

where UT,kl​a​tU^{lat}_{T,k} is independent noise.

For a source table TT (no FKs), the mechanism omits the selection step and outputs

ZrT,k=ψTs​r​c​(ΦTc​t​x​({Au}u∈P​ac​t​x​(T,k)),UT,kl​a​t),UT,kl​a​t∼Unif⁡(0,1),Z_{r_{T,k}}=\psi^{src}_{T}\!\left(\Phi^{ctx}_{T}(\{A_{u}\}_{u\in Pa^{ctx}(T,k)}),\ U^{lat}_{T,k}\right),\quad U^{lat}_{T,k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1),

with a table-shared map ψTs​r​c\psi^{src}_{T}.

Theorem D.22 (Completeness of Stage 2 (Structure)).

Fix a schema GSG_{S}. Let P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}) be any structural distribution satisfying Assumptions D.16, D.17, D.18, D.19, D.20. Then there exists a parameter setting of the above selective SCM such that the induced distribution over (𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵)(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}) approximates P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}) arbitrarily well in distribution.

Proof.

Step 1 (Reduction to local kernels). By Corollary D.21 (candidate-based factorization), it suffices to approximate each local conditional

P(ZrT,k,UT,k|CtxT,k,{ϕT,k(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1),P\!\Big(Z_{r_{T,k}},U_{T,k}\ \Big|\ \mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},S_{T,k-1}\Big),

with the convention that for source tables UT,kU_{T,k}, 𝒞T,k\mathcal{C}_{T,k}, and ST,k−1S_{T,k-1} are empty.

Step 2 (Sampling representation + approximation transfer). Fix a dependent table TT and step kk. Define the (pre-selection) input

XT,k≔(CtxT,k,{ϕT,k​(c)}c∈𝒞T,k,ST,k−1),YT,k≔(UT,k,ZrT,k).X_{T,k}\ \coloneqq\ \Big(\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k},\ \{\phi_{T,k}(c)\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}},\ S_{T,k-1}\Big),\qquad Y_{T,k}\ \coloneqq\ (U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}).

Since 𝒞T,k\mathcal{C}_{T,k} is finite and ZrT,k∈ℝdZ_{r_{T,k}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}, the product space 𝒞T,k×ℝd\mathcal{C}_{T,k}\times\mathbb{R}^{d} is standard Borel. By Lemma D.5, there exists a measurable sampler fTf_{T} and an independent UT,k(g​e​n)∼Unif⁡(0,1)U^{(gen)}_{T,k}\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1) such that

(UT,k,ZrT,k)​=𝑑​fT​(XT,k,UT,k(g​e​n)).(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}})\ \overset{d}{=}\ f_{T}(X_{T,k},U^{(gen)}_{T,k}).

Thus, if our model class contains f^T\hat{f}_{T} with f^T​(XT,k,UT,k(g​e​n))→fT​(XT,k,UT,k(g​e​n))\hat{f}_{T}(X_{T,k},U^{(gen)}_{T,k})\to f_{T}(X_{T,k},U^{(gen)}_{T,k}) in probability under the induced input law, then the induced conditional law converges in distribution.

Step 3 (Realizability by the structural SCM parameterization). Write the target local kernel as

P⁡(UT,k,ZrT,k∣XT,k)=P⁡(UT,k∣XT,k)⋅P⁡(ZrT,k∣XT,k,UT,k).P(U_{T,k},Z_{r_{T,k}}\mid X_{T,k})=P(U_{T,k}\mid X_{T,k})\cdot P(Z_{r_{T,k}}\mid X_{T,k},U_{T,k}).

Because 𝒞T,k\mathcal{C}_{T,k} is finite, any categorical distribution P⁡(UT,k∣XT,k)P(U_{T,k}\mid X_{T,k}) can be represented by logits {ℓc​(XT,k)}c∈𝒞T,k\{\ell_{c}(X_{T,k})\}_{c\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}} via

P⁡(UT,k=c∣XT,k)=Softmax​({ℓc′​(XT,k)}c′∈𝒞T,k)c,P(U_{T,k}=c\mid X_{T,k})=\mathrm{Softmax}(\{\ell_{c^{\prime}}(X_{T,k})\}_{c^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}_{T,k}})_{c},

e.g., by taking ℓc​(XT,k)=log⁡P⁡(UT,k=c∣XT,k)\ell_{c}(X_{T,k})=\log P(U_{T,k}=c\mid X_{T,k}) (up to an additive constant). Choosing the scoring network gg from a universal approximator class over its inputs and using the candidate embeddings ϕT,k​(c)\phi_{T,k}(c) yields arbitrarily accurate approximation of these logits under the induced input law.

Conditioned on (XT,k,UT,k)(X_{T,k},U_{T,k}), the latent distribution P⁡(ZrT,k∣XT,k,UT,k)P(Z_{r_{T,k}}\mid X_{T,k},U_{T,k}) admits a measurable sampler from uniform noise by Lemma D.5. Choosing the update map ψ\psi from a universal approximator class yields an arbitrarily accurate approximation of this sampler in probability under the induced input law.

Finally, Assumption D.20 restricts dependence on the structural information to hierarchy-respecting processing. Choosing ΦTc​t​x\Phi^{ctx}_{T} and ΦTc​a​n​d\Phi^{cand}_{T} from universal hierarchy-respecting function classes yields arbitrarily accurate approximations of CtxT,k\mathrm{Ctx}_{T,k} and ϕT,k​(c)\phi_{T,k}(c) as required.

Step 4 (Conclude). Combining (i) approximation of the categorical selection kernel for UT,kU_{T,k} and (ii) approximation of the conditional sampler for ZrT,kZ_{r_{T,k}} yields a sequence of structural SCM parameters whose induced local conditionals converge in distribution. Substituting these approximations into the Stage 2 factorization and using independent per-step noise variables gives convergence of the induced Stage 2 distribution to the target. ∎

D.3.3 Universality of the Three-Stage Construction

Theorem D.23 (Universality of the three-stage construction).

Let 𝒫R​D​B\mathcal{P}_{RDB} be the family of relational database distributions P⁡(𝒟)P(\mathcal{D}) that factorize as

P⁡(𝒟)=P⁡(GS)​P​(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)​P​(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS),P(\mathcal{D})=P(G_{S})\,P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})\,P(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S}),

and satisfy the Stage 2 assumptions and Stage 3 assumptions stated above.

Assume: (i) the schema model family {P^θS​(GS)}\{\hat{P}_{\theta_{S}}(G_{S})\} is dense in distributions over finite schema DAGs; (ii) for each fixed schema GSG_{S}, the Stage 2 family {P^θ2​(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)}\{\hat{P}_{\theta_{2}}(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})\} is dense in the admissible P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}); and (iii) for each fixed (GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵)(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}), the Stage 3 family {P^θ3​(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)}\{\hat{P}_{\theta_{3}}(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})\} is dense in the admissible P⁡(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)P(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S}).

Then the composite family

P^θ​(𝒟)=P^θS​(GS)​P^θ2​(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)​P^θ3​(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)\hat{P}_{\theta}(\mathcal{D})=\hat{P}_{\theta_{S}}(G_{S})\,\hat{P}_{\theta_{2}}(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})\,\hat{P}_{\theta_{3}}(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})

is dense in 𝒫R​D​B\mathcal{P}_{RDB} (in distribution).

Proof sketch.

Fix any target P∈𝒫R​D​BP\in\mathcal{P}_{RDB} and ε>0\varepsilon>0.

Choose θS\theta_{S} so that P^θS​(GS)⇒P⁡(GS)\hat{P}_{\theta_{S}}(G_{S})\Rightarrow P(G_{S}). Next, for each fixed schema GSG_{S}, choose θ2​(GS)\theta_{2}(G_{S}) so that P^θ2​(GS)​(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)⇒P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)\hat{P}_{\theta_{2}(G_{S})}(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})\Rightarrow P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S}). Finally, for each fixed (GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵)(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}), choose θ3​(GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵)\theta_{3}(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}) so that P^θ3​(GS,𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵)​(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)⇒P⁡(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS)\hat{P}_{\theta_{3}(G_{S},\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z})}(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S})\Rightarrow P(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S}).

The joint law is the iterated mixture

P⁡(𝒟)=∫P⁡(GS)​∫P⁡(𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵∣GS)​P​(𝒟d​e​p∣𝒟s​t​r​u​c​t,𝒵,GS),P(\mathcal{D})=\int P(G_{S})\int P(\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z}\mid G_{S})\,P(\mathcal{D}_{dep}\mid\mathcal{D}_{struct},\mathcal{Z},G_{S}),

and P^θ​(𝒟)\hat{P}_{\theta}(\mathcal{D}) is defined by the same iterated mixture with each factor replaced by its approximation. Since weak convergence is preserved under forming such mixtures on standard Borel spaces, P^θ​(𝒟)⇒P​(𝒟)\hat{P}_{\theta}(\mathcal{D})\Rightarrow P(\mathcal{D}). ∎
